name: ESP32 DevKit V1
description: High-performance 240MHz dual-core Xtensa 32-bit MCU with integrated Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, Bluetooth v4.2 BR/EDR, and BLE.
realWorldAnalogy: High-performance 240MHz dual-core Xtensa 32-bit MCU with integrated Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, Bluetooth v4.2 BR/EDR, and BLE.

hazards: All GPIO pins operate strictly at 3.3V logic - 5V inputs will damage the chip!

wiringGuidance: Power via Micro-USB or 3.3V pin. When connecting 5V Arduino sensors, use a resistive voltage divider or logic level shifter on signal lines.
commonMistakes: Applying 5V logic signals directly to ESP32 input pins.
Trying to use GPIO 34, 35, 36, or 39 as outputs—they are input-only pins!

miniExperiment.title: ESP32 Wi-Fi Scanner
miniExperiment.expectedOutput: Serial Monitor (at 115200 baud) lists the number of nearby 2.4GHz Wi-Fi networks detected.
